To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a joint machine learning (ML) and game theory (GT) modeling (MLGT)-based RC method can achieve better R-D performances and quality smoothness than the state-of-the-art methods.

the proposed joint machine learning and bargaining game theory framework is capable of achieving the performance close to the performance of FixedQP method, while the proposed framework has much lower computational complexity than the FixedQP method.

the proposed MLG-based RC method achieves better R-D performances and quality smoothness than the other state of the art one-pass RC methods and the achieved R–D performances are very close performance limits of the FixedQP method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a novel MLGT-based RC algorithm for HEVC.
the design of an efficient and practical rate allocation scheme for HEVC video coding, where the rate allocation scheme is formulated as a game-theoretic optimization problem.
a joint machine learning, and game theory modeling for rate control in high efficiency video.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed joint machine learning and bargaining game theory-based RC method can effectively improve the coding performance of HEVC.
the proposed MLG-based RC method can significantly outperform the other state-of-art RC methods in R-D performances, bit rate control, buffer control, and quality smoothness.
the proposed MLGTCBRC method is a very promising one-pass RC scheme for HEVC, and the proposed MLGTM method is a very effective and efficient tool for one-pass RC in HEVC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MLGT framework can be used to improve the performance limits of video coding, especially for HEVC, by overcoming the “chicken-andegg” dilemma and improving the prediction accuracy of the R-D model.

the MLGT-based RC framework is a promising approach for future video coding standard, such as the next generation HEVC, to achieve high R-D performance and quality smoothness with high coding efficiency.
the proposed ML-GT framework is a promising approach to achieve the optimal rate control performance for the future video coding standard.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MLGT framework is a promising approach for the future video coding RC optimization.

the proposed joint machine learning and bargaining game-based RC method can effectively overcome the “chicken-andegg” dilemma in HEVC video coding, and achieve better R-D performances than the state-of-the-art RC methods.
ML and game theory can be combined to achieve better R-D performances in video coding.
